title: Aqueous Droplets Used as Enzymatic Microreactors and Their Electromagnetic Actuation
protocol: Hydrophobize magnetic nanoparticles by adding 0.85 g FeCl3 hexahydrate and 0.30 g FeCl2 tetrahydrate to 200 mL water/ethanol solution (4:1 v/v).
Add 0.20 mL PFOTES with vigorous stirring at 500 rpm in an inert gas atmosphere.
Adjust the pH of the solution dropwise to 8 using an ammonium hydroxide solution (1.5 M).
Stir the mixture for 24 hours.
Separate magnetic particles from the solution using a bar magnet.
Pour out the supernatant while keeping the magnet attached to retain the particles.
Wash the particles three times with water/ethanol solution using a bar magnet.
Dry the particles at 60 °C for 24 hours.
Grind dried particles slightly using a glass pestle.
Place the ground particles directly in a weighing pan (46 × 46 × 8 mm, polystyrene).
Pipette 10 µL reaction solution onto all the particles.
Move the weighing pan slightly in a circular way for approximately 10 s.
Store remaining particles at room temperature for further applications.
Build a 5 µL microreactor with water on a teflon film.
Analyze the contact angle using an optical contact angle measurement device according to manufacturer's instructions.
Design double coil bodies with a height of 16 mm, diameter of 10 mm, and inner diameter of approximately 4 mm by using CAD software.
Print the coil bodies with a 3D printer using polylactide filament.
Wrap the bodies with a 0.08 mm copper wire to achieve 4,500 windings using a computer controlled winding machine.
Arrange double coils in a matrix on an electric board with a Peltier element underneath.
Screw on the double coils and connect them to a control via ribbon cable.
Add an iron core or neodymium magnet to the coil body depending on the desired magnetic field strength.
Place a quartz glass plate with a maximum height of 1 mm on the coil matrix.
Activate the coil containing a neodymium magnet to open and close microreactors as needed.
Use neodymium magnets to merge two microreactors that are initially about 10 mm apart by activating the coils for approximately 25 seconds.
Switch on the Peltier element beneath the coil matrix to cool down the reaction solution in the microreactor and decrease the coil temperature.
Dissolve horseradish peroxidase at a concentration of 0.1 µg/mL in potassium phosphate buffer (0.1 M, pH 6.5).
Dilute 10-acetyl-3,7-dihydroxyphenoxazine with potassium phosphate buffer (0.1 M, pH 6.5) to a final concentration of 200 µM.
Use 10 µL of each solution to build two microreactors as described in 2.2).
Merge the two microreactors using magnetic forces (neodymium cylinder magnet: 12.5 mm x 4 mm, 1,035 kA m-1) at 25 °C.
Position a fluorescence probe with an excitation wavelength of 570 nm and an emission wavelength of 585 nm approximately 10 mm directly above an opened microreactor before the merge.
